legal_counterexamples: Healthy 2.4145 GiB Native versus Web 2 is already present. Browser rounding, clamps, unavailable APIs and process/environment limits are legitimate counterexamples to equality.
next_action: A later version may test a semantic range/residual; first bind units and actual browser-version behavior. No new bound implemented here.

next_action: Keep existing single-field pilot result; any Native CPU-count collection requires separate authorization.

units_and_meaning: Native Locale.getDefault().toLanguageTag() is process default; Web languages is an ordered array. V1 numeric control retains only length.
legal_counterexamples: Application/process locale, browser language preferences, fallback language tags and ordering can legitimately differ. en-US,en still includes native en-US.
next_action: Consider a bounded language-family/set relation after authorizing B and agreeing legitimate customization cases; no arbitrary string vocabulary.

units_and_meaning: Native language subtag en versus Web full tag en-US; raw equality has mismatched granularity.
legal_counterexamples: Regional variants and per-application language are legitimate; current language field stays en-US even in French languages-list intervention.
next_action: Keep as explanatory evidence; any new normalization grammar is B-only.

units_and_meaning: Native rawOffset/60000 is standard-time local-minus-UTC minutes without DST; JavaScript getTimezoneOffset is UTC-minus-local at current date.
legal_counterexamples: DST, different sampling instant near transitions and legitimate per-process/browser timezone changes invalidate simple equality or sign reversal.
next_action: Resolve current-time/DST semantics and allowed customization before a B predicate. Existing GMT-only data cannot validate nonzero/DST cases.

legal_counterexamples: Distinct IDs can identify the same offset; equal current offsets can have different DST rules.
next_action: Do not learn literal zone IDs. Bind semantic equivalence and date if later authorized.
